title: Chloral Hydrate Seed Clearing
author: Gabrielle Sandstedt
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bakaicse

steps.title: Emasculate bud and pollinate
steps.instruction: Remove the anthers from a selected bud (emasculation). After 2–3 days, pollinate the emasculated flower by self‑fertilization, outcrossing, or leave it unfertilized to develop fruit.

steps.title: Harvest developing fruit
steps.instruction: Collect the developing fruit 1–5 days after pollination (or 2–3 days after emasculation). This captures early seed development (0–5 days) before the seed tissue thickens.

steps.title: Prepare Hoyer's and diluted solutions
steps.instruction: Make Hoyer's solution by mixing 19 g gum Arabic, 12 g glycerol, 250 g chloral hydrate, and 75 mL water. For the diluted solution, combine 7.5 mL of the Hoyer's solution with 2.5 mL of 10 % gum Arabic to obtain 10 mL total.

steps.title: Mount ovules on slide
steps.instruction: Place 10 µL of the diluted Hoyer's solution on a clean glass slide. Using sharp forceps, dissect the ovules from the harvested fruit directly onto the droplet.

steps.title: Add cover slip and refrigerate
steps.instruction: Pipette approximately 30 µL of the diluted Hoyer's solution over the dissected ovules, gently place a coverslip on top, then lay the slide flat and upright in a 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Clear and image ovules
steps.instruction: Allow the slide to clear for at least 1–12 hours, depending on ovule development stage, before observing the samples with a Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) microscope.
